title: Foundations & Architecture
description: Execution pipeline: compilation, bytecode (.class), JVM runtime mechanics, and the JIT compiler.

title: Language Basics & Data Types
description: Reference for the 8 Java primitives, memory sizes, value ranges, identifier rules, and type inference with var.

title: Control Flow & Logic
description: Reference: Dynamic runtime branching with if, else if, else, ternary expressions, short-circuit evaluation, and control flow guarantees.

title: Methods & Modular Code
description: Reference: Method declaration anatomy, Call Stack frames, return semantics, and Java strict Pass-By-Value evaluation model.

title: Arrays & Memory Structure
description: Reference: Fixed-size indexed contiguous heap buffers, memory layout (header, length, elements), default initialization, bounds checking, and O(1) random access.

title: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) Essentials
description: Reference: Class definitions, heap object allocation, stack reference pointers, Compressed OOPs, static vs instance fields, and GC eligibility.

title: OOP Inheritance, Polymorphism & Abstraction
description: Reference: IS-A inheritance hierarchies via extends, super() chaining, method overriding rules, covariant return types, and final modifiers.

title: Modern Java Language Features
description: Reference: Type-safe constant singletons, java.lang.Enum class hierarchy, constant-specific method bodies, and high-performance EnumSet/EnumMap bit vectors.

title: Exception Handling
description: Reference: The Throwable class tree, distinction between fatal JVM Errors and recoverable Exceptions, stack trace unwinding, and printStackTrace mechanics.

title: Generics & Collections Framework
description: Reference: Compile-time type parameterization (<T>), diamond operator (<>), bounded type parameters (T extends Number), and JVM type erasure mechanics.

title: Functional Programming & Streams
description: Reference: Anonymous function syntax (->), Single Abstract Method (SAM) contracts, @FunctionalInterface, invokedynamic bytecode execution, and java.util.function taxonomy.

title: File I/O, NIO.2 & Date/Time
description: Reference: Java classic I/O (java.io), Byte Streams vs Character Streams, 8KB buffer decorators (BufferedReader/BufferedWriter), explicit UTF-8 encodings, and flush/close lifecycle.

title: Concurrency & Multithreading
description: Reference: Operating system platform threads (1:1 kernel mapping), the six Thread.State lifecycle stages, daemon threads, joining, and cooperative interruption.

title: JVM Internals & Memory Architecture
description: Reference: JVM memory architecture (Heap, Metaspace, Stack Frames, PC Register, Native Stack), Stack vs Heap mechanics, and JSR-133 Happens-Before formal invariants.

title: Reflection, Annotations & JPMS
description: Reference: Declarative metadata via @interface, meta-annotations (@Retention, @Target, @Inherited, @Repeatable), permitted element types, and reflection parsing.

title: Data Access & Build Tools
description: Reference: java.sql architecture (Connection, PreparedStatement, ResultSet), SQL injection mitigation via parameterized placeholders, transaction boundaries (setAutoCommit), and batch execution.

title: Web Architecture & The Jakarta EE Evolution
description: Reference: Historic evolution from J2EE/Java EE to Eclipse Jakarta EE, package namespace migration from javax.* to jakarta.*, and application server runtime compatibility matrices.

title: Web Containers & Packaging
description: Reference: Web Application Archive (WAR) anatomy, the protected WEB-INF boundary, web.xml vs annotations, Catalina container hierarchy, and Tomcat deployment pipelines.

title: Servlet API Architecture & Request Handling
description: Reference: jakarta.servlet.Servlet interface lifecycle phases (init, service, destroy), container thread-pooling model, and instance-variable concurrency hazards.

title: State Management, Filtering & Security
description: Reference: HTTP statelessness mitigation, HttpSession lifecycle, JSESSIONID tracking mechanics, secure cookie flags (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite), and session concurrency.

title: Server-Side Rendering with JSP & JSTL
description: Reference: JavaServer Pages translation lifecycle into HttpJspPage servlets, directive syntax, scriptlet elimination, and the 9 implicit runtime objects.

title: Enterprise Web Applications & Data Flow
description: Reference: Model-View-Controller architectural separation in server-side Java, Front Controller dispatching, and request-scoped model binding.

title: Modern Jakarta EE Specifications
description: Reference: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM) fundamentals, EntityManager lifecycle states (Transient, Managed, Detached, Removed), dirty checking, and 1st-level cache.

title: Spring Core & Inversion of Control
description: Explore the architectural foundation of the Spring Inversion of Control (IoC) container, comparing the lightweight BeanFactory with the enterprise-ready ApplicationContext, lazy vs eager instantiation, and contextual infrastructure.

title: Spring Boot Architecture & Configuration
description: Deconstruct Spring Boot's opinionated architecture: condition evaluation algorithms, starter dependencies, META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports, and embedded web servers (Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow).

title: RESTful Web Services & Global Error Handling
description: Architect resilient, production-grade REST APIs using Spring Web MVC: HTTP method mappings (@GetMapping to @DeleteMapping), URI template variables (@PathVariable), query parameters (@RequestParam), payload deserialization (@RequestBody), and explicit HTTP status code semantics via ResponseEntity<T>.

title: Persistence with Spring Data JPA & Databases
description: Explore the architectural foundation of Spring Data JPA, covering the cohesive repository interface hierarchy, dynamic runtime proxy generation, entity lifecycle states, and automated snapshot-based dirty checking.

title: Enterprise Security with Spring Security 7
description: Understand the modern security architecture in Spring Security 7 (Spring Boot 4.1): declarative SecurityFilterChain bean configuration, URL authorization matchers, lambda DSL, stateless CSRF semantics, and production password hashing with BCrypt and Argon2.

title: Master Annotations Reference Dictionary
description: The definitive, cross-referenced architectural dictionary categorizing and comparing core annotations across Java SE Core, Jakarta EE enterprise specifications, and the Spring Boot production ecosystem.

title: Production Libraries & Distributed Systems
description: Eliminate repetitive boilerplate in enterprise Java applications using Project Lombok's annotation processor and MapStruct's compile-time, type-safe bean mapping engine.

title: Advanced Persistence, Dynamic Queries & Auditing
description: Build type-safe, dynamic search queries in Spring Data JPA using JpaSpecificationExecutor and Specification<T>, composing complex multi-criteria boolean expressions without string concatenation.

title: Enterprise Identity & OAuth2 / OIDC Architecture
description: Configure Spring Security 6 as a stateless OAuth2 Resource Server: asymmetric RS256 token validation using remote JWK Sets (JWKS), custom JwtAuthenticationConverter for role extraction, and realm claim mapping.

title: Asynchronous, Distributed Scheduling & Batch Processing
description: Decouple long-running operations from HTTP threads in Spring Boot: @EnableAsync, custom ThreadPoolTaskExecutor tuning, saturation policies, CompletableFuture aggregation, and AsyncUncaughtExceptionHandler.

title: Real-Time Web & Asynchronous Streaming
description: Build real-time full-duplex communication in Spring Boot: WebSocket handshake, STOMP sub-protocol messaging, in-memory and external message brokers (RabbitMQ/ActiveMQ), @MessageMapping, and SimpMessagingTemplate.

title: Relational Database Essentials & SQL
description: Master core relational concepts: tables, columns, rows, primary keys, foreign keys, relationships (1:1, 1:N, M:N), and normalization.

title: Polyglot Persistence & NoSQL Systems
description: Compare relational and non-relational database architectures: tabular models vs document stores, ACID vs BASE, and CAP theorem trade-offs in distributed systems.

title: ACE & MQ Basics
description: Understand the distinct roles of IBM MQ as message transport and ACE as integration broker and data transformer.

title: ESQL Reference
description: Overview of Extended Structured Query Language (ESQL), its runtime lifecycle, and the entry-point Main() function.

title: Connecting Nodes to MQ
description: Configure an integration node default queue manager using mqsicreatebroker -q, startup dependencies, and headless mode.

title: IBM MQ Commands
description: Launch the interactive IBM MQ Script Command (MQSC) console to manage queues, channels, and listeners.

title: ACE Administration Commands
description: Initialize environment variables and system PATH using mqsiprofile.cmd to run mqsi commands in standard shells.

title: BIP Codes Reference
description: Searchable matrix of IBM ACE BIP diagnostic codes: understand severity suffixes (I, W, E), causes, and fixes.

title: Message Flow Patterns & Node Selection
description: Decision guide: choose between Compute (ESQL), JavaCompute (Java), and Mapping Node (Graphical Data Map) in ACE.
